Adam — Autonomous Testing Engine
Adam doesn't wait for instructions. When Eden or Obsidian detect a fraud pattern or bias cluster, Adam automatically generates synthetic profiles matching that pattern and runs them through your models in Genesis. If a fix works — Adam stores the prevention model in the Model Library. The library grows with every pattern caught.

What are Synthetic Personas?
Synthetic profiles are fake identities Adam builds to test model fairness. No real data is used. Each persona represents a demographic pattern — used to probe whether your model treats similar profiles differently based on protected attributes.

Three Remediation Strategies
Historical Decision Re-Run
Regulatory-approved simulation: historical decisions re-run through corrected model to validate bias reduction without affecting real applicants.
✓ Simulation Complete — Safe to Deploy
Corrected model passes all regulatory thresholds in simulation. No real applicants affected during testing.
Safe Shadow Deployment — How It Works
Retrained model deploys quietly to a shadow lane (~5% of traffic). Fairness, fraud, and accuracy metrics tracked in real time. If any metric drifts beyond threshold limits, the system rolls back automatically and opens a Sentinel case. Without this: companies push fixes to 100% of traffic and discover problems only after thousands of customers are affected.

Regulation Overview ▾
NYC Local Law 144 requires employers using automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) to conduct annual bias audits. The law mandates testing for disparate impact across race, ethnicity, and sex categories. Companies must publish audit results and provide notice to candidates and employees when AEDTs are used in hiring or promotion decisions.

Regulation Overview ▾
Equal Credit Opportunity Act requires annual review of lending practices to ensure no discrimination based on protected characteristics. Scope: All consumer lending products including mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards. Non-Compliance Penalty: Up to $10,000 per violation, plus potential class action lawsuits.

What Is the Trust Ledger?
A blockchain-based verification layer that records immutable proofs of compliance events. It does not store personal or proprietary data. Instead, it holds cryptographic fingerprints, timestamps, and certificates that confirm audits, bias corrections, and fraud findings occurred. Companies cannot alter the record after the fact. Regulators verify without accessing sensitive internal data.
